verdict.rationale: MotherDuck has no first-party sandbox feature in the evidence, but you can assemble a safe test setup from other pieces. You can develop locally in DuckDB before moving to the cloud (docs-18). The local MCP server can run against local DuckDB files (docs-22), and dbt targets switch with just the `path:` setting (docs-7). Agents can be restricted to read-only MCP access (docs-31), and every user or agent gets an isolated compute instance (docs-59). Missing for 10: a dedicated sandbox or staging environment, zero-copy cloning or branching of production databases, and documented guidance or hands-on corroboration for agent test isolation.
